source.title: Tracking Universal Features Through Fine-Tuning and Model Merging

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tracks sparse-autoencoder features through fine-tuning and model merging. It does not measure neuron poles, assign neurons main jobs, or test neuron explanations in the sense of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported feature-persistence, case-study, and automated-interpretability results concern sparse-autoencoder features, not the neuron-pole job counts in the claim. They are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. The paper cites work on explaining neurons but reports no result testing V1–V7.
record.test_reason: The study tracks sparse-autoencoder features across fine-tuning and SLERP merging in one-layer Transformers. It reports no neuron-level job shares, no neuron explanations or scores, no InceptionV1 analysis and no neuron attribution graphs. Its automated-interpretability scoring (Bills et al. style) is applied to SAE features, not neurons, so it is a related but different construct. It cites Bills et al. (2023), one original source, only for the prompt format.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that very few features persist between models, but persisting ones are interpretable (punctuation, formatting). They also find that SLERP merging maintains features of the parent models, and that features are diluted through fine-tuning and merging. They call for scaling to deeper models and other domains. The record's phrase 'most base-model features disappear' matches §4.1.
record.recipe_differences: The study tracks SAE-feature activation-pattern correlations and manually or automatically interprets selected features; it does not audit neuron poles or count neuron jobs. Models are one-layer Transformers fine-tuned on Lua or TinyStories and merged.
record.method_sensitivity: The study uses an 80% activation-pattern correlation threshold to define persistence; it notes that this threshold was based on manual inspection. It selects the merged model at t = 58% based on validation accuracy balance.

fits_no_version.finding: Few SAE features persist across domain fine-tuning and merging. Persisting features include punctuation (20%) and formatting (5%) features. An assignment feature persists (mean cross-correlation 85.1%), while a Python-exception feature disappears (40.81% correlation to the closest Lua feature).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in small Transformers mostly do not persist through domain fine-tuning and merging; generic syntactic features tend to persist.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-4 Turbo simulation scores for SAE-feature explanations are shown as Pearson correlation distributions (figure only). The text says they closely match Bricken et al.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Simulation-based explanation scores for SAE features in a one-layer model resemble those reported by Bricken et al. (2023).

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and weights will be available upon publication.
record.problems: The experiments use small, one-layer models and limited domains; the authors state that the findings may not generalize to larger and more diverse corpora. The automated-explanation correlation results are plotted without textual numerical values. Feature persistence depends on the stated 80% correlation threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed neuron-pole claim versions were reported. Model next-token accuracy across the interpolation path is not extracted because it concerns merging performance rather than neuron-pole interpretability.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares (one job, two related jobs, not yet understood).
Neuron job shares across other dense and mixture-of-experts models and scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization and tools cause messy neurons, and how the interpretable share changes with better tools.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
Whether neuron explanations built from activating examples predict where the neuron fires.
Simulation-based scores for neuron explanations. Only SAE features are scored here.

record.verdict_notes: The gate decision of cites_only/T6 is confirmed. The study's only contact with the claim is the Bills et al. explanation and simulation pipeline, applied to SAE features rather than neurons. It therefore does not bear on V7's neuron-level minority-of-good-scores claim. Even for SAE features, no shares or thresholds are given in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares of one job, two related jobs, and not-yet-understood poles.
Neuron-pole job shares across other models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
The proposed causes of messy neurons and the estimates for interpretable neurons in InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons and their reconstruction error.
Whether explanations of individual neurons predict their firing beyond the activating examples used to form them; the study instead evaluates explanations of SAE features.
Automated scores for neuron explanations and the share of neurons with good scores; the study scores SAE-feature explanations instead.
